title: Tamsin and the Orchard
premise: In 1847, in the river town of Marlow Bend, Tamsin Ashgrove completes the atlas her dead master bled for, believing maps record the world and never change it. But when census taker Elias Vane asks about a household that officially never existed — the Ashgrove orchard cottage and the foundlings raised there — she discovers the town's founding families erased a flood, a fire, and eleven orphaned children from every record to protect their land claims. Racing the spring thaw that will open the river to the victors' hired historians, Tamsin must gather testimony from the scattered survivors, now grown and hiding in plain sight, and engrave the truth into the atlas plates themselves. She succeeds at terrible cost: the atlas is published with both maps, the lie and the truth side by side, and Tamsin finally understands she was one of the eleven all along.
about_author: Freya Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal records in river towns, where she learned that every official history has a shadow ledger. She writes historical fiction about the people who keep records — and the people the records were built to forget.

chapters.title: The Last Plate
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the winter of 1847, she engraves the final map plate of Master Hollis's unfinished county atlas, alone in his cold workshop. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; she believes finishing the atlas is the last duty owed to the dead.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Census taker Elias Vane arrives to verify households and lingers on the orchard cottage, asking who owned it before the Ashgroves. His pen hovers; Tamsin lies for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: unease, the first crack in her belief that paper is neutral.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Searching Hollis's papers for provenance notes, she finds a sealed letter addressed to 'the eleventh child' and a page razored out of the parish register. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into curiosity she cannot put down.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Ferry
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, brief ferry-woman interlude. Crossing the half-frozen river to question old Brida Ferris, Tamsin is told: 'Ask about the winter of '31, girl, then decide if you want the answer.' Emotional beat: first contact with the hidden network of survivors.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In Hollis's desk she finds a child's copybook listing eleven names, each struck through except one — an initial: T.A. Emotional beat: vertigo; the list feels like a mirror she isn't ready to look into.

chapters.title: The Founders' Dinner
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Invited to present the atlas to Marlow Bend's founding families, she watches magistrate Corven praise 'a town without tragedy' while his daughter Merrit watches Tamsin with open hostility. Emotional beat: the victors' version of history, delivered as hospitality.

chapters.title: Brida's Testimony
chapters.summary: Brida's POV (framed as dictated testimony). The winter of '31: the ice dam broke, the mill burned the same night, and eleven children of the drowned laborers' row were dispersed by the founders 'for their own good.' Emotional beat: testimony as act of courage after decades of silence.

chapters.title: The Erasure
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Cross-checking maps, deeds, and registers, she proves the laborers' row was removed from every document — including two plates of Hollis's own atlas, altered under pressure before he died. Emotional beat: betrayal; even her master complied, and she must decide what he died for instead.

chapters.title: Merrit's Warning
chapters.summary: Merrit Corven's POV. Merrit confronts Tamsin: her father knows what Hollis was doing, and historians arrive when the ice breaks. She offers Tamsin a place in the new order if she burns the copybook. Emotional beat: temptation wrapped in threat; Merrit is not simply cruel.

chapters.title: The Orchard Cottage
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She finally searches the cottage cellar and finds eleven small initials carved in the wall — and recognizes her own hand among them, though she has no memory of carving it. Emotional beat: the ground gives way; her childhood is a constructed story.

chapters.title: Hollis's Letter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She breaks the seal: Hollis took her in as the eleventh child, hid her origins even from himself in guilt, and left the atlas deliberately unfinished so someone would have to choose whether to finish it honestly. Emotional beat: grief reframed — the atlas was always a test.

chapters.title: Gathering the Eleven
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. With Brida's help she locates the scattered survivors: a schoolmistress, a convict, a respected alderman who denies everything. Emotional beat: hope and resistance in equal measure; some survivors prefer the erasure.

chapters.title: The Alderman's Denial
chapters.summary: Alderman Pike's POV. One of the eleven, now wealthy and respectable, explains why he signed the founders' affidavit: memory is a luxury of the unruined. Emotional beat: chilling self-justification; the antagonist within the victims.

chapters.title: Ice Sounds
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The river begins to groan and shift; word comes that Corven has engaged historians from the capital, arriving by the first boat. Emotional beat: the clock becomes audible; every scene now races the thaw.

chapters.title: The Schoolmistress's Slate
chapters.summary: Schoolmistress Ada Quill's POV. She kept a secret teaching slate recording the true names of the drowned parents, risking her post for twenty years. She agrees to testify. Emotional beat: quiet heroism; ordinary people keeping dangerous truths alive.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Under Brida's gentle questioning, fragments surface: smoke, a woman singing, being carried across ice. Emotional beat: identity dissolving and reforming; she mourns the orphan-story she was given and fears the one she's recovering.

chapters.title: Corven's Offer
chapters.summary: Magistrate Corven's POV. He summons Tamsin, reveals he knows exactly who she is, and offers patronage, publication, and a place in town history — if the atlas omits the row. Emotional beat: seduction of legitimacy; the devil quoting her own ambitions back to her.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She refuses, and Corven moves: the workshop lease is revoked, Brida's ferry license 'under review,' Ada dismissed. Emotional beat: the cost of truth arrives immediately and lands on everyone she loves.

chapters.title: The Copybook Goes Missing
chapters.summary: Elias Vane's POV. The census taker, revealed as a quietly principled man investigating the '31 discrepancies on his own initiative, finds the copybook stolen from Tamsin's rooms — and suspects Merrit. Emotional beat: an unexpected ally inside the machinery of records.

chapters.title: Merrit Unmasked
chapters.summary: Merrit's POV. Cornered by Elias, Merrit admits she stole it — not for her father, but because she was the ninth child, raised as a Corven ward, and cannot bear either truth existing. Emotional beat: antagonist revealed as the story's most wounded soul.

chapters.title: Two Sisters of the Row
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Merrit, alternating short sections. The two women confront each other across the copybook: same origin, opposite survival strategies. Emotional beat: recognition without reconciliation; the theme of chosen versus assigned identity made flesh.

chapters.title: The Engraver's Gambit
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She resolves to cut a supplementary plate — a second map showing the laborers' row, the flood line, and eleven names — and bind it into every atlas copy before the historians dock. Emotional beat: resolve; the plan crystallizes around her craft.

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Ada and Brida's alternating POV. The survivors mount a watch rotation to guard the workshop and feed the furnace; the town notices lights and whispers spread. Emotional beat: found family assembling itself around a shared act of witness.

chapters.title: The Convict Returns
chapters.summary: Joss Renner's POV. The tenth child returns from the penal colony, hard and bitter, refusing to help until Tamsin shows him the carved initials — his own among them. Emotional beat: rage meeting evidence; the hardest recruit bends.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Someone cracks the press screw and salts the acid bath; the workshop survives on luck and Joss's repair skills. Emotional beat: paranoia and siege mentality; the enemy is inside the town walls.

chapters.title: Pike's Price
chapters.summary: Alderman Pike's POV. Corven pressures Pike to swear a fresh affidavit denying the row existed; Pike hesitates over the blank line, remembering his mother's voice. Emotional beat: the collaborator's crisis; the affidavit scene as moral fulcrum.

chapters.title: The Blank Line
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Pike comes to the workshop at night, not to confess but to ask what name should go where his signature would be. Tamsin tells him the truth needs no signature, only witnesses. Emotional beat: mercy extended to the unworthy; the theme of belonging tested.

chapters.title: First Boat Sighted
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The ice breaks early; the historians' steamer is two days out. The plate is half-engraved. Emotional beat: panic compressed into craft; Tamsin works with bleeding hands.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Corven's men seize the workshop and the finished atlases; Tamsin hides the supplementary plates in the orchard cellar, beneath the initials. Emotional beat: loss and defiance; the building falls but the archive of hands holds.

chapters.title: Trial by Record
chapters.summary: Public hearing, multiple brief POVs (Brida, Ada, Joss, Merrit). Corven stages an inquiry to legitimize the erasure before the historians arrive; testimony collides with affidavit. Emotional beat: public reckoning; the town forced to listen to itself.

chapters.title: Merrit Breaks
chapters.summary: Merrit's POV. Called to corroborate her father, Merrit instead reads the eleven names aloud from the stolen copybook, returning it to Tamsin on the inquiry floor. Emotional beat: the climax's human detonation; betrayal of family for the sake of truth.

chapters.title: Corven's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Corven's POV. He produces Hollis's altered plates as proof the master himself endorsed the official map, arguing the atlas is settled history. Emotional beat: the victor nearly wins on technicality; documents cut both ways.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Child Speaks
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin testifies, presenting Hollis's sealed letter and her recovered memories, declaring herself the eleventh child and the atlas's true executor. Emotional beat: claiming identity publicly; the private wound becomes public record.

chapters.title: The Historians Dock
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The steamer arrives; the lead historian, a dry woman named Professor Ilsa Maren, refuses to accept either side's summary and demands primary evidence. Emotional beat: suspended judgment; the arbiters are neither saviors nor enemies but strict.

chapters.title: The Cellar Evidence
chapters.summary: Tamsin, Merrit, and Joss escort Maren to the orchard cellar: initials, the hidden plates, Ada's slate, Brida's sworn dictation. Emotional beat: the archive of the powerless laid bare; material truth against institutional narrative.

chapters.title: Both Maps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Maren rules the atlas must be published with both plates — the official map and the engraved truth — or not at all. Corven, facing exposure, withdraws rather than let the inquiry continue. Emotional beat: victory that costs; no one is fully redeemed.

chapters.title: The Binding
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the repaired workshop, the found family binds the atlases together, sewing the second plate into every copy by hand through the night. Emotional beat: communion through labor; the book as covenant.

chapters.title: Publication Day
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. The atlas sells; some buyers tear out the second plate, others frame it. Pike signs a public retraction of the affidavit. Emotional beat: truth released into the world, no longer hers to control.

chapters.title: The Orchard in Bloom
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Spring: the eleven survivors plant a tree for each parent in the orchard cottage garden. Merrit stays in town, estranged from her father but not from Tamsin. Emotional beat: mourning turned cultivation; belonging chosen, not granted.

chapters.title: Cartographer's Note
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, closing. She pens the atlas's final page: a note explaining why two maps exist, and that every map is an argument. She signs it with her full recovered name. Emotional beat: resolution and authorship of self; history happens to her, and she answers back.
